What to look for

This is issue #2331: a switch over an `enum class` value that covers EVERY enumerator and
has NO `default:`, inside a non-void function.  The fall-off-the-end path is lowered to an
LLVM `unreachable`, which is not a legal DXIL instruction, so the shader fails DXIL
validation.  Nothing is signed, because nothing valid was produced.

The DXC panes are expected to FAIL, not to compile.  Look for:

    error: validation errors
    error: Instructions must be of an allowed type.
    note: at 'unreachable' in block '#4' of function 'MainPS'.

Exit is E_FAIL (0x80004005) -- an ordinary diagnosed error, not a crash.

The 1.6.2112 pane also prints "DXIL.dll not found.  Resulting DXIL will not be signed",
because Compiler Explorer runs Linux builds with no validator DLL beside them.  That is
incidental: validation still runs, and still rejects this shader, in both panes.

Two things to try in the editor:
  * add `default: return MyCB.m_color;` to the switch -- it compiles, which is the
    reporter's workaround, and is why this is about an absent `default:` rather than about
    enums or about signing;
  * delete any one `case` -- since v1.5.2010 that is a clean front-end error
    ("control may reach end of non-void function [-Wreturn-type]"), reached long before
    the validator.  Only the fully-covered switch still gets through to it.

No clang pane: clang's HLSL backend rejects this shader for an unrelated reason (a backend
error about lowering the buffer access) that it also produces for inputs DXC accepts, so a
clang pane here would show a failure that has nothing to do with this issue.  On a
cut-down form clang can compile, it emits no `unreachable` at all.  See the triage notes.

Compiler Explorer runs Release builds and its oldest DXC is 1.6.2112, so it corroborates
the local evidence rather than dating anything: the local bisection covers v1.4.1907 on.
